hypothesis: Every park of any core stops WDT0 renewal and leaves a retained record, within the stated instruction, byte and memory budgets, in host and instruction-emulation checks.
prediction: Budgets (baseline -> budget, measured by): parks that end in a reboot: EL1 faults that stop a supervised service, or on core 0 (counted) -> every park on each of the 8 cores (vector fault, deliberate exit, EL3-origin entry, failed validation), checks/reset-latency.c with services.c and the modeled watchdog, one injected case of each kind per core. Request to watchdog expiry: unbounded for a core without a supervised service -> at most 4.02 s (one 20 ms pass plus 4 s), same model with a park at each phase of the renewal second. Fields per record: ESR_EL1 only (counted) -> kind, status, detail, vector slot, counter, epoch, and for vector faults four EL1 registers and the task name, decoded by checks/fault-capture.py; a deliberate exit with a stale x2 decodes as an exit. Capture cost: the existing EL3 report from validation to publication is about 36 instructions (counted) -> pending byte within 6 instructions of the MPIDR decode, capture at most 250, no stack, MMIO or lock, writes only the core's slot and byte (Unicorn with modeled system registers; memory-write log). Supervisor cost per 20 ms pass 0 -> one 64-bit load, no lock or barrier (disassembly of board_resident_renew). Boot rotation none -> 1,152 bytes read, 1,160 bytes written to RAM and 1 KiB cleared once per boot, no added cache maintenance. USB0 report none -> one 1,160-byte response in 1 tick (checks/usb0-service-burst.py, 1,160-byte row). Single-core fault line 3 registers -> at most 160 bytes, patch applies with fuzz 0 (build of every target that compiles platform.c). Memory none -> no new reservation, 1 KiB of .result and 1,168 bytes of .bss, code at most 1 KiB (nm sizes). No hot path changes apart from the supervisor's load. No interrupt is added: the supervising task already polls every 20 ms, and an SGI would shorten a 4 s path by at most 20 ms.

conclusion: Every reboot and capture budget is met. Two figures exceed their budgets. The rotation reads the stage-2 header words and each valid slot twice (once to check magic and CRC, once while copying), exceeding the 1,152-byte read budget by up to 232 bytes; it runs once per boot, before any secondary core starts. The 1,152 budget assumed one read per slot plus the 128-byte resident result. .bss exceeds its 1,168-byte budget by 112 bytes (the 72-byte larger USB0 frame, the stop-detail word and alignment). The EL3 path to publication grows from 122 to 203 or 224 instructions, which runs only when a core parks; the supervisor pass grows from 40 to 52 instructions (one plain load and the expired-service index, as designed). The single-core images' 1 KiB of .text growth carries no budget; platform_exception formats the record through a733_fault_line and a733_fault_line_hex, which print SPSR_EL1, the core number and the task name in addition to the three registers. No interrupt, wake-up, lock, barrier on the supervisor path, cache maintenance or copy on a hot path is added. Board evidence remains outstanding.
narrative: Results table (metric: base / changed / budget). Modeled parks that end in a reboot: 1,000 of 8,000 (core 0 only) / 8,000 of 8,000 / every park on every core. Park to watchdog expiry: unbounded on cores 1..7 / at most 3.999 s / 4.02 s. Park entries that store the pending byte: 0 of 72 / 72 of 72 (9 kinds on 8 cores) / all. Instructions from MPIDR decode to pending store: no store / 6 / 6. Capture leaf: none / 85 / 250. Stack, MMIO or lock use: none. Fields per record: ESR_EL1 as detail / 11 for an EL1h vector fault, 10 for EL0 / as designed. EL3 entry to record publication: 122 / 203 deliberate exit, 224 vector fault / no budget. Supervisor pass: 40 instructions, no pending load / 52 instructions, one plain ldr, no barrier or atomic / one load. Rotation, once per boot: 1,868 to 1,875 instructions; bytes read in the check's slot mix 1,248 without and 1,384 with the copied resident result against 1,152; written 1,160 to RAM and 1,024 cleared in .result against 1,160 and 1 KiB. USB0 report: 1,160 bytes in 1 tick, 3 packets. Single-core fault line: 3 registers / at most 136 bytes, 4 registers, core and task / 160 bytes (the design's implementation notes cite 137). Single-core patch applies with fuzz 0, offset 25 lines. OS image .text 845,856 -> 846,880 (+1,024); .rodata / .data 41,353 / 3,168 unchanged; .bss 1,463,136 -> 1,464,416 (+1,280) against +1,168; no new reservations, .result stays 16 KiB. Single-core image .text 492,224 (crypto) and 490,432 (PWM), +1,024 in each. Size growth by nm symbols: .bss +1,280 = a733_fault_previous 1,160, a733_fault_pending 8, USB0 frame buffer 1,088 -> 1,160 (+72), supervisor stop-detail word 8, 32 bytes of section alignment; the heap's device pool shrinks by 1,280 so the RAM footprint is unchanged. .text +1,024 = a733_fault_boot 388, a733_fault_capture 340, board_resident_renew +48, board_resident_stop_detail 12, supervise +16, services state function +124, USB0 exchange +72, a733_cached_prepare +4, and vector-table markers padded to section alignment. Single-core platform.c grows from 1,546 to 2,551 bytes. Rotation read count in the check's mix includes eight slot reads of 128 bytes, a second read of every slot that passes magic and CRC while copying it, and two stage-2 report header words. Measured rotation for the implementation notes: 1,875 instructions, 968 bytes read with no valid slot. Review hashes: the three review hashes of continue.S in cmake/ name the new file; platform/a733-storage-maintenance/continue.patch and platform/a733-smp-observe/continue.patch apply without fuzz; images without SUNSTONE_A733_FAULT_PAGE assemble byte-identical continue.S, continue.c and tasks.c objects. Capture constraints: slots occupy 0x42001000-0x42001400 inside the 16 KiB .result reservation at 0x42000000 (resident result ends at 0x42000080, native startup records start at 0x42002000, memtest uses 0x42003000); EL1 keeps no mapping of the monitor block (memory.c clears a733_cached_el1_l2[16]). Barriers: DSB SY after the pending byte; DMB OSHST between slot fields and magic; DSB SY after the magic before the parking WFE; none on the reader (one relaxed 64-bit load). Task-name read accepts a TCB pointer only when 8-byte aligned and the name lies inside 0x41200000-0x42000000 (a733_extent_within in include/a733_range.h). Rejected reboot sequences (the standing constraint is one WDT0 writer, mode 0x41, configuration 1, output 2, no disarm): a short interval, as the pinned board kernel sunxi_wdt.c (wdt_v103, sunxi_wdt_restart) writes mode interval 0 (0.5 s) with enable then restarts, adds a second WDT0 writer and a mode value that the contract checks reject, to save at most 3.5 s on a path followed by a multi-minute slot load; a software reset, as the pinned bootloader b791be84 arch/arm/mach-sunxi/board_sun60iw2.c (sunxi_board_reset_cpu) writes WDT_SRST_REG, which manual section 8.3.6.3 requires the watchdog timer to be disabled for, forbidden by the resident contract. No PRCM system-reset register appears in the manual. RTC general-purpose registers (section 9.1.7.14) survive reset, but bootloader rtc.c uses indices 0, 2 and 6 and the boot0 owners of the remaining indices are unknown, so they are not used. Armed state: A733 User Manual V1.00 section 8.3.6.5 (configuration 01 resets the whole system) and the loader sequence in docs/boot-slots.md. Left out because no consumer: an SGI to the supervisor, a USB0 reboot command, slot capture of EL3-origin exceptions (they stop renewal and keep the existing monitor report), stack or register dumps, and fault capture in the QEMU platforms. Not proven by a pinned source: that an SMC leaves x2, ESR_EL1, ELR_EL1, FAR_EL1 and SPSR_EL1 unchanged, and the single-copy atomicity of byte stores; both come from the Arm Architecture Reference Manual (DDI 0487), which is not pinned. TF-A 0892ad4d arch.h (pinned under cpu-entry/) supplies the ESR_EC_SHIFT and SPSR_M positions the decoder uses. Failure classes: all parks are section 1.8 class 3 (the core parks at EL3 and keeps every lock, buffer and DMA job until reset); other cores run for at most 4.02 s and the OS image writes no storage; a stalled supervisor or bus hang stops renewal and leaves no slot, as do an EL3-origin entry and a failed validation, and the next boot reports these resets as unexplained; a cold boot and a watchdog reset cannot be distinguished because no retained reset-cause register is known (docs/watchdog-reset-evidence.md).

hypothesis: WDT0 expiry in the resident lifetime reboots into a cold boot, the fault slots survive it, and the next boot reports a real fault's registers over USB0.
prediction: Four steps, each in a scheduled board session under docs/validation.md. 1. WDT0 expiry in the resident lifetime reboots into a cold boot (shared with the watchdog expiry trial). 2. The slots at 0x42001000 survive WDT0 reset and boot0's DRAM initialization with a valid CRC; the stage-2 loader's copy of the previous result relies on the same unproven retention. 3. A deliberate load from an unmapped address in a test task, once on an A55 and once on an A76, produces the expected ESR_EL1, ELR_EL1 and FAR_EL1. 4. The previous-boot report arrives over USB0 after the reboot.
conclusion: Not yet run. Expiry and cold reboot, slot retention across reset and the registers of a real fault are unproven on the board.
